messages:
maya: Heads-up—noticed a ~12% p99 increase in host-side latency after the kernel-selector v2 rollout (region: us-west1). Looks concentrated in tokenization + ingress path.
jon: ugh. any obvious diff in allocations or syscall counts?
alice: I ran a quick perf; syscall writev count up ~3x for grpc streams, also smallwrite spikes on 512-1k payloads. KV-cache hit rates steady.
maya: That's what I saw too. KV hit stable, but pretokenizer is emitting more fragments (weird UTF8 normalize path length).
sam: Can you paste the flamegraph snippet?
maya: Sure — small snippet from perf (top hot functions):
```
host_parse_frame
-> tokenizer_normalize_utf8
-> tokenizer_slice
-> grpc_writev_coalesce
-> host_proxy_flush
```
jon: grpc_writev_coalesce being hotter suggests we lost coalescing after switching kernel variant? maybe batching heuristics changed request pacing.
alice: I compared request inter-arrival histograms pre/post: median same, but tail shows more microbursts (~5-15ms buckets) which prevents effective batching.
maya: microbursts align with kernel selection change that moved some models to fast-decoder kernel (lower decode CPU) — but it changed host-side scheduling timers.
sam: So model->kernel mapping change changed scheduling/timer tick alignment and now many small writes escape coalescing window.
jon: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) revert kernel mapping for affected models in us-west1 2) widen writev coalesce window by 2ms 3) add temporary pretokenizer debounce for fragments.
maya: I'm for (1) as fastest rollback. (2) might help but could increase latency for low-TPS requests.
alice: I can prototype debounce in pretokenizer: if token boundary < 3 bytes and next frame arrives within 2ms, merge. cheap hack.
perf-ci-bot: Performance regression alert: job/host-ingress-p99 increased by 13% on canary. See: https://perf.redwood/compare/1732109990..1732110000
jon: Good to have that link. maya — can you trigger a canary revert for kernel mapping? deploy-bot, can we do a fast revert to previous selector?
maya: I'll open a rollback PR now and kick canary.
maya: PR: revert-kernel-selector-v2 -> rolling canary in us-west1.
maya: (added small log patch to increase writev coalesce window to 2ms in proxy as well)
sam: After patch, we should run a synthetic microburst workload: run 'microburst-runner --payload 800 --iatt 3-20ms --qps 200' against canary.
alice: I'll run that and post results in 10m.
jon: Longer term: we should make kernel selector emit scheduling hints to host-proxy (e.g., debounce_hint) so coalescing/batching adapts to kernel choice.
maya: Agree — filed issue: https://redwood/issue/INF-4721 — notes: kernel->scheduling-hint surface + add telemetry for writev coalescing misses.
jon: Also let's add KV-cache eviction/pressure markers to traces so we can correlate. Current KV metrics miss short-lived pressure.
maya: Test results: alice — any update?
alice: Ran microburst workload against canary + debounce patch: p99 host latency dropped ~9% vs pre-patch canary, writev syscalls down 40%, flamegraph shows tokenizer_normalize still present but grpc_writev_coalesce reduced.
maya: Nice. Can we cut a canary promote if no regression in next hour?
sam: I'll watch e2e 30m window. also adding a canary that only widens coalesce window (no kernel revert) to measure tradeoff.
jon: Action items: maya rollback PR + monitor, alice run extended microburst tests and attach traces, sam run coalesce-only canary, I will spec kernel->scheduling-hint API.
maya: Thanks team. tagging follow-ups in INF-4721. :thumbsup:
